# Problem 1 · Which streams get pulled hardest toward the mean? (simulation)

> Simulate 24 streams with unequal effort (8 each at 2, 5 and 30 visits;
> `set.seed(413)`, true $\tau = 12$, $\sigma = 20$, $\mu = 80$). (a) Predict by
> hand the retention weight $B_i = \tau^2/(\tau^2 + \sigma^2/n_i)$ for 2 and 30
> visits. (b) Fit `lme(Density ~ 1, random = ~ 1 | Stream)`, extract
> $\hat\tau, \hat\sigma$, and tabulate mean |no-pooling − partial| by effort
> group. (c) Explain why the formula behaves this way. (d) Find the most extreme
> 2-visit stream and say which estimate you would report. (e) Reply to the
> proposal to drop every stream with fewer than 5 visits.

**My work:**

```{r}
library(nlme)
set.seed(413)
nvisit <- c(rep(2, 8), rep(5, 8), rep(30, 8))
tau <- 12;  sig <- 20;  mu <- 80
stream_mean <- rnorm(length(nvisit), mu, tau)
Streams <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(nvisit), function(i)
  data.frame(Stream = factor(i),
             Density = rnorm(nvisit[i], stream_mean[i], sig))))
m <- lme(Density ~ 1, random = ~ 1 | Stream, data = Streams)
nopool  <- tapply(Streams$Density, Streams$Stream, mean)
partial <- coef(m)[, 1]
n_i     <- as.numeric(table(Streams$Stream))
# Your B_i calculations and the table for (b) here
```

# Problem 3 · Where does the fish-to-fish variation go? (simulation)

> Simulate 12 fish at ages 1 to 8 (`set.seed(77)`; fish-to-fish SD of
> $L_\infty$ = 12, measurement error = 3) and fit `nls` (one curve for all) and
> `nlme` (random $L_\infty$). (a) Report the three SDs and say which fit
> recovers both sources. (b) Work out where the wrong `nls` sigma comes from
> using the fraction $1 - e^{-\kappa a}$. (c) Describe the `nls` residual plot
> and say what is actually wrong with the model. (d) Compare the standard
> errors of Kappa and Tzero between the fits. (e) Re-run with `nfish` = 4 and
> 20 and report the estimated fish-to-fish SD.

**My work:**

```{r}
set.seed(77)
nfish <- 12; ages <- 1:8
Kap <- 0.25; T0 <- 0
sd_Linf <- 12; sd_obs <- 3
Linf_i <- rnorm(nfish, 100, sd_Linf)
sim <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:nfish, function(i) data.frame(
  Subject = factor(i), Age = ages,
  Length  = Linf_i[i]*(1-exp(-Kap*(ages - T0))) + rnorm(length(ages), 0, sd_obs))))
gd <- groupedData(Length ~ Age | Subject, data = sim)
fit_nls  <- nls(Length ~ Linf*(1-exp(-Kappa*(Age-Tzero))), data = sim,
                start = c(Linf=100, Kappa=.2, Tzero=0))
fit_nlme <- nlme(Length ~ Linf*(1-exp(-Kappa*(Age-Tzero))),
                 fixed = Linf + Kappa + Tzero ~ 1, random = Linf ~ 1 | Subject,
                 data = gd, start = c(Linf=100, Kappa=.2, Tzero=0))
# Your comparisons here
```

# Problem 4 · Trophic position: a random-effect structure the data cannot support (qcbs_w6_data.csv)

> Fit M1, M3, M4, M7 and M8 and rank them with `aictab()`. (a) Why are Lake and
> Fish_Species random-effect candidates, and what would push you the other way?
> (b) Write the bivariate Normal implied by `(1 + Z_Length | Fish_Species)` and
> count its parameters. (c) Report the table, then run `isSingular()` on all
> five fits. (d) Read the correlation off `VarCorr(M8)`, run the two
> three-point simulations, and explain which parameter broke and why. (e) Fit
> `M8u` with the `||` form and compare its SDs with M8's. (f) Decide which model
> to report and justify it. (g) Say when you would switch species to a fixed
> effect and what that costs.

**My work:**

```{r}
M1 <- lmer(Z_TP ~ Z_Length + (1|Fish_Species) + (1|Lake), data=dat, REML=TRUE)
M3 <- lmer(Z_TP ~ Z_Length + (1|Fish_Species), data=dat, REML=TRUE)
M4 <- lmer(Z_TP ~ Z_Length + (1|Lake), data=dat, REML=TRUE)
M7 <- lmer(Z_TP ~ Z_Length + (1|Fish_Species) + (1+Z_Length|Lake), data=dat, REML=TRUE)
M8 <- lmer(Z_TP ~ Z_Length + (1+Z_Length|Fish_Species) + (1|Lake), data=dat, REML=TRUE)
aictab(list(M1=M1, M3=M3, M4=M4, M7=M7, M8=M8))
sapply(list(M1=M1, M3=M3, M4=M4, M7=M7, M8=M8), lme4::isSingular)
# Your VarCorr(M8), the three-point simulations, and M8u here
```
